Leah — quick answers inline and some concrete artifacts attached. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

> 1) Can you confirm whether any Redwood-hosted persistence (e.g., KV cache, prefix cache, or audit logs) could contain raw PHI by default, or if that can be configured off?

- KV/prefix caching: configurable. By default we enable prefix caching for performance on hosted models, but for PHI workloads caching can be disabled at a route or model-level. When caching is enabled we offer TTLs and strict encryption-at-rest.
- Audit logs: operational logs may contain metadata about requests (latency, token counts) and redacted request IDs. Full request payloads are not retained in plain text in hosted. For Dedicated and Private patterns we can configure longer or shorter retention and include customer-controlled log ingestion.

> 2) For Dedicated deployment: does Redwood offer single-tenant physical isolation (i.e., dedicated GPU pool) with an option to disable shared cache primitives?

- Yes. Redwood Dedicated provides tenant-isolated GPU pools and an option to disable shared/cache primitives. That setup + a signed BAA is the typical path customers take to run PHI workloads without using the multi-tenant hosted API.

> 3) SOC 2: do you have a copy of your latest control summary / testing period we can share with our audit team?

- We completed a SOC 2 Type II engagement in Q2 2026; I’ve attached the control summary and can provide the auditor letter under NDA.

Attachments included in this message: RDW_security_control_summary_Q2_2026.pdf (control summary), RDW_BAA_draft_v1.docx (same as prior), SoCo_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (filled where applicable).

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Confirm engineering dataflow diagram showing where PHI may traverse and mark all configurable knobs (cache, telemetry, log retention) — will send by Tue 11/24 EOD.
- Start an internal legal thread to iterate RDW_BAA_draft_v1 and prepare a DocuSign envelope so your team can review quickly.

Thanks — talk soon.
